output.subject: We've received your complaint about your check order
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us about your check order. We have received your complaint and want to make sure we have understood it correctly.

You told us that you ordered checks through our website on September 18 and paid $28.00. You mentioned that when the checks arrived, they were printed with an address that is not yours and never has been, even though you have lived at your current address for six years. You said this means you cannot use the checks. You have asked us to reprint them at no charge and to explain how that address came to be on your order.

We understand how frustrating it is to pay for something and then find you can't use it, and we're sorry for the inconvenience this has caused.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days. If there is anything you'd like to add in the meantime, please reply to this email.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Confirm the September 18 online check order and the $28.00 charge.
Compare the address printed on the checks with the address on file and the address submitted with the order.
Check whether the address on file was ever changed. An unfamiliar address could signal unauthorized account changes.
Decide whether to offer a reprint at no charge. The draft only acknowledges the request.
Determine what explanation can be given for how the address got on the order.
Consider advising the customer on securely destroying or returning the unusable checks.
The customer's phone number was left out of the draft; confirm their preferred contact method if needed.
